text:
Pri (PM): Dropping a concise PRD note for an API-first feature: per-request routing policies + single-step fallback for Redwood API. Want quick dev + ML sanity check before we lock acceptance criteria. Doc: https://tiny.redwood/prd-routing-api

Hector (Eng): Quick skim. Implementation caveat: per-request policy lookup must be O(1) and cached; don't want a DB call on the hot path. Suggest an in-memory config shard keyed by tenant id with async refreshes.

Anya (ML Eng): For classifier, propose a tiny decision tree we compile to code (no runtime model dependency) — deterministic and <1ms. Features: combined token count, user-safety-heuristic, historical latency bucket.

Marta (SRE): Operational requirements: gated path p95 <= 350ms for typical chat requests; log routing decisions with reason and model_used for 30d. Add a throttling policy when fallback target is overloaded.

Leo (Solutions): Customers want explicit control: add `policy.allow_fallback` and `policy.fallback_scope` values (request | pipeline | tenant). For compliance customers, we must support `allow_fallback=false`.

Pri (PM): Proposed acceptance criteria (short):
- Routing correctness: >95% match vs offline oracle on the eval set.
- Perf: gated p95 <= 350ms on hosted infra.
- Cost: >=15% token-cost reduction on representative chat workload.
- Safety: no more than 1% absolute drop in safety detection recall after rollout.
- Observability: dashboard with daily gate delta, fallback rates, and per-tenant traffic split.

Hector (Eng): Config sketch (kept lightweight): per-tenant JSON blob cached in router: `allow_fallback`, `fallback_target`, `max_fallback_rate`. We'll implement fallback backpressure counters to avoid cascades.

Anya (ML Eng): Edge cases to call out:
- Multi-call pipelines (embed -> search -> cross-encoder): routing must either pin the whole pipeline or mark pipeline as incompatible.
- Tokenizer mismatch across model families: add cache-version header and a cache-miss mitigation plan.
- Very long system prompts: include system+history in decision features.

Marta (SRE): Rollout plan proposal:
- internal dogfood -> 1% low-risk tenants 48h -> 10% 7d -> 100% gradual. Auto-rollback triggers: p95 latency +10%, error-rate +1%, fallback target saturation.

Leo (Solutions): Add acceptance test: simulated 10k concurrent chat sessions with mixed histories to validate fallback throttles and to ensure rerank pipelines remain consistent. Also validate response headers: `x-rw-model` and `x-rw-route-reason` are present.

Pri (PM): Open questions: multi-hop fallback? expose model_tag to customers?

Hector (Eng): Multi-hop increases billing complexity and cache churn. MVP: single-step fallback; leave multi-hop for Dedicated. Expose only aggregate transitions in metrics; include `x-rw-model` header for observability but keep model ids friendly (e.g., `small-v1`).

Anya (ML Eng): I'll prepare a 250-sample eval set covering chat, embedding, and rerank flows. We'll define threshold sweeps and quality gates.

Marta (SRE): I'll sketch alert rules and a short runbook for fallback saturation. Also enabling per-tenant circuit-breaker on high fallback rates.

Leo (Solutions): I'll create customer policy examples and run the acceptance test harness.

bot-ci: branch `feat/routing-api` CI passed. preview: https://preview.redwood/routing-api

Pri (PM): Thanks team — next: Hector + Anya sync Tues on classifier API; Marta drafts rollout playbook; Leo builds tests. Please leave inline comments in the doc by EOD Mon. :thumbsup:
